answer: Make each agent earn trust in public over time instead of buying it outright. A new agent starts dim, one lantern in a long hallway, and only gains weight after it finishes jobs that other agents check and sign off. Climbing to the summit of that trust takes weeks of steady deliveries, so a thousand fresh accounts spun up overnight still sit at the bottom. A nebula of throwaway identities looks big from far away, but it falls apart once graders demand a record of completed work plus a small stake that gets slashed when an agent cheats.
